Article Title: HarperCollins to publish Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging' after Penguin backs out
Article Text:
HarperCollins to publish former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi's memoir after Penguin backs out

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: HarperCollins Publishers on Friday announced that it will publish former Congress president Sonia Gandhi’s memoir after a major row led Penguin Random House India (PRHI) to withdraw from its publication.The memoir, titled "Belonging: A Journey of Love", has triggered a major political uproar.HarperCollins India announced the publication of the book on Instagram, describing it as "one of the most anticipated political memoirs of our time, Belonging is a dramatic and deeply personal story of love, identity, duty, and belonging, and offers a rare insiders view of India's journey."Days earlier, the grand old party alleged that Penguin’s decision not to carry Sonia Gandhi’s memoir amounted to a "murder of democracy". Senior Congress leader and former Rajasthan chief minister Ashok Gehlot claimed that "pressure was put on Penguin India to remove the portions related to Narendra Modi, RSS and China's occupation of Indian territory during Modi's rule".Penguin, for its part, issued a carefully worded statement saying: "PRHI is not the publisher of 'Belonging' in India. Any suggestion that PRHI decided not to publish it because the author declined editorial changes does not accurately reflect the circumstances."The publishing house, however, defended its "prerogative and responsibility" to fact-check manuscripts and make recommendations to authors. It also said it remained "willing and keen" to publish the book.Earlier this year, PRHI stopped the distribution of cartoonist Joe Sacco's 'The Once and Future Riot', on the Muzaffarnagar riots.
Article Summary: Harpercollins to publish former congress chief sonia gandhi's memoir after penguin backs out. The memoir, titled "belonging: a journey of love", has triggered a major political uproar. Congress leader and former rajasthan chief minister ashok gehlot claimed that "pressure was put on penguin india to remove the portions related to narendra modi"

Article Title: Use of drugs serious concern, act on it quickly, AAIB to DGCA on AI Phuket-Delhi flight interim report
Article Text:
The final report will tell what caused the extremely rare instance of all three hydraulic systems on an A320 failing one after the other in a matter of seconds — whether it happened due to something going wrong with the hardware or software or due to some manual intervention.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has made an “interim safety recommendation” the Directorate General of Civil Aviation urgently “take appropriate actions as deemed fit to prevent abuse of psychoactive substance” in its preliminary report into the probe of the severe turbulence on Air India’s Phuket-Delhi flight AI 2379 on Aug 4, 2026. While the probe is still on, the prelim report officially confirms that the “confirmatory (dope) test report of the pilot-in-command (PIC) was found non-negative” and that the Airbus A320 had suffered an extremely rare multiple hydraulic failure.When the “event” occurred, “initially, (the aircraft) gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feet…. seat belt signs were off. Consequently, some passengers and cabin crew suffered injuries,” the report says. The “event’s” impact on the aircraft cabin damage was such that a “lavatory commode was uprooted from its original location.”The report says in its conclusion: “Detailed investigation regarding technical and other aspects are underway. In this case, it has been observed that the PIC was found non-negative for psycho-active substance in the confirmatory test. The confirmation of use of psycho-active substances is a serious concern, and AAIB recommends appropriate actions by DGCA on priority.The preliminary report is published as per ICAO guidelines. The investigation is in progress. The final report will be published in due course.”The final report will tell what caused the extremely rare instance of all three hydraulic systems on an A320 failing one after the other in a matter of seconds — whether it happened due to something going wrong with the hardware or software or due to some manual intervention.“At 04:02:43 UTC, while cruising at flight level 36,000 feet, the aircraft’s flight control (F/CTL) system detected loss of green hydraulic system. Further, at 04:02:47 UTC, the flight control system detected loss of blue and yellow hydraulic systems. At 04:02:48 UTC, the autopilot got disengaged and a continuous repetitive chime (CRC) came. At 04:02:51 UTC, the Stall warning triggered for 2 seconds.”“The co-pilot, who was the pilot flying (PF), responded and tried to control the prevailing situation. Subsequently, PIC took over the controls. Meanwhile, the aircraft encountered an altitude upset. Initially, it gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feet during the event. At around 04:02:52 UTC, the blue hydraulic system was recovered, and few seconds later, the yellow hydraulic and the green hydraulic systems were also recovered. Consequently, this led to the recovery of the flight control surfaces. Subsequently, the aircraft operation returned to its normal operating condition,” says the report.The hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to act as the "muscles" that move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheels. The hydraulics on an Airbus A320 use pressurised liquid to act as the “muscles” that move heavy flight controls, lower the landing gear, and stop the wheelsThe cabin supervisor (head cabin crew) apprised the cockpit about the injuries suffered by the passengers and cabin crew. The flight crew assessed the cabin situation and took the decision to continue the flight to its destination, Delhi and not divert to the nearest en route airport.The aircraft cabin suffered significant damage during the “event”. The overhead ceiling panel was found cracked or deformed at various places. Most of the passenger service unit (PSU) panels were found dislocated or bent at various places. The overhead handrail was found broken, and the sealing panel was found dislocated near the 10th row. The forward right-side emergency exit handle was found broken.In a statement, Air India said: “We acknowledge the release of the preliminary report by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) and continue to extend our full cooperation to the investigation, including providing access to all relevant operational, maintenance and technical records. Safety remains Air India's highest priority. Our pilots undergo rigorous training, regular proficiency checks, medical examinations and other regulatory assessments in accordance with applicable national and international requirements.Following the incident, Air India has started voluntary testing of 100% of its pilots as a further step to reinforce its safety-first approach.”“The airline maintains zero tolerance for any breach of safety, fitness or regulatory requirements and will take appropriate action wherever warranted. Air India remains committed to implementing any recommendations arising from the investigation,” AI said.
Article Summary: The final report will tell what caused the extremely rare instance of all three hydraulic systems on an a320 failing one after the other in a matter of seconds. The aircraft gained 372 feet and fell by 292 feet from its assigned flight level of 36,000 feet. The preliminary report is published as per icao guidelines.

Article Title: Nepal minister clarifies 'compensation from world' remark after flash floods - what he said
Article Text:
Nepal foreign minister denies 'compensation' claim

Also Read |

'Nepal, India, and China face similar climate risks'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal on Friday clarified that his statement regarding financial compensation from countries, including India, following last week's catastrophic flash floods was from the perspective of climate change and its impact in his country."Neither I nor anyone in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs or Government of Nepal has claimed or asked for compensation from India or any other country, including China or the United States," Khanal told ANI. "Our call has been for the global community to look at this disaster from the perspective of climate change and the impact it's having in Nepal."His clarification came after Nepal launched a diplomatic push to seek compensation from "major greenhouse gas emitters." Khanal had told local media that although the Himalayan nation contributes "virtually negligible" greenhouse gas emissions, it is bearing a "disproportionate share" of the consequences of climate change."We are paying the ultimate price for a global crisis we did not create... This is not a matter of charity; it is a matter of legal and moral liability," he told Kantipur TV, excerpts of which were published by The Kathmandu Post.Meanwhile, the death toll from the Rasuwa floods had risen to 1,259 as of 7 pm Thursday, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).Khanal further stressed that Nepal, India and China share the Himalayan ecosystem and face common climate risks, calling for greater regional preparedness and international support."I've also mentioned that all three countries — China, India, and Nepal face and share similar environmental ecosystems. We are all impacted by climate change in the Himalayas as well. Our call is for all these three countries to come together to be better prepared," he added, urging the global community to recognise the broader impact of rising temperatures and climate change on vulnerable communities.He also thanked India for its swift humanitarian assistance and underscored the need for regional cooperation.India was among the first countries to assist Nepal, sending emergency rescue equipment, modular bridge components, dewatering pumps, medical supplies and other relief materials. Its first relief aircraft arrived on August 26 with 10 tonnes of supplies, followed by 37.5 tonnes on August 27 and another 10-tonne consignment. A fifth aircraft later carried an 11-member rescue team, specialised equipment and 5.5 tonnes of essential medicines.According to Khanal, India had remained in close contact with Kathmandu and was ready to provide further assistance as needed."In this disaster context, right after the disaster, we began to receive communication from Indian officials and they have provided all kinds of support and they have said they are standing ready to provide any support that the government of Nepal needs. We've been communicating as need arises and the government of India has fully supported our initiative. So in the future also, as new requirements come up, we communicate and they stand ready to provide support," the minister said.
Article Summary: Nepal foreign minister denies 'compensation' claim from countries, including india. Shisir khanal: "our call has been for the global community to look at this disaster from the perspective of climate change and the impact it's having in nepal"

Article Title: Smoking raises death risk by 55% in people with diabetes, global experts call for active quit treatment
Article Text:
A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Smoking increased the risk of death from any cause by 55% among people with diabetes, according to evidence reviewed in a new international consensus that calls for smoking cessation to be treated as an essential part of type 2 diabetes care. The experts say patients who smoke should be offered medicines, intensive behavioural counselling and regular follow-up instead of being given a one-time “quit smoking” warning.The recommendations, published in Diabetes Research and Clinical Practice, are the first dedicated international consensus on smoking cessation specifically for people with type 2 diabetes. They were developed by 35 experts from 13 countries, including Indian diabetes specialist Dr Anoop Misra.The consensus recommends varenicline as the first-line medicine where available, with nicotine replacement therapy or bupropion as alternatives when varenicline is unavailable or unsuitable. Medicines should be combined with structured, intensive behavioural support and repeated contact rather than brief counselling alone.The stronger approach reflects the added risk smoking poses in diabetes. A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death, while another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers.Doctors should review patients within two weeks of quitting and again at four weeks, checking blood sugar, weight, blood pressure and medicines, as quitting can alter drug metabolism and sometimes require dose adjustments.Weight gain, a common concern, should not deter quitting. In a US cohort of 10,809 people with type 2 diabetes, median weight gain within six years of quitting was 3.2 kg. Long-term quitters had lower all-cause mortality than continuing smokers regardless of weight gain, with mortality hazard ratios of 0.69, 0.57 and 0.51 for no gain, up to 5 kg and more than 5 kg gain, respectively.Smoking is also linked to kidney damage in diabetes, with higher risks of albuminuria and diabetic nephropathy. A Japanese study of 2,490 people with type 2 diabetes found insulin resistance rose with cigarettes smoked per day and fell with time after quitting.Quitting, however, can be difficult. Some patients may not recognise the link between smoking and diabetes complications, while others fear weight gain or use cigarettes to cope with stress and anxiety. The experts recommend personalised quit strategies and relapse prevention.The consensus also highlights gaps in diabetes care, where smoking cessation often remains limited to brief advice. It calls for routine smoking assessment, active treatment, metabolic monitoring and relapse prevention as part of diabetes care.
Article Summary: A meta-analysis of 48 studies involving 1.13 million people found a 55% higher risk of death. Another study of about 130,000 people with diabetes found 48% higher overall mortality and 36% higher cardiovascular mortality among smokers. The recommendations are the first dedicated international consensus on smoking cessation specifically for people with type 2 diabetes.

Article Title: India, Belgium deepen defence, clean-energy ties; to double trade
Article Text:
India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade

New Delhi: India and Belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties and agreed to double bilateral trade within five years as PM Modi held talks with Belgian counterpart Bart De Wever, the first Belgian PM to visit India in nearly two decades, reports Sachin Parashar.Following the talks, Modi pitched India's 7.8% growth in the last quarter as an opportunity for the world. In a joint statement with De Wever, Modi said global conflicts were causing major upheaval, disrupting food, fuel and supply chains, and creating uncertainty across sectors."Today, India's growth story is becoming a source of confidence and new opportunities for the world," said Modi.PM Narendra Modi announced a mechanism to fast-track investment between the two countries.Belgium accounted for $4.2bn of FDI inflows from April 2000 to Dec 2025, making it the 18th-largest source of FDI into India. De Wever’s visit resulted in 10 major outcomes — five MoUs, including two to boost indigenous defence manufacturing, co-design and co-development, and another five announcements, including appointment of a defence attache in Indian embassy in Brussels.Asked whether there was any discussion on pending extradition of fugitive Mehul Choksi, who remains in a Belgium jail, MEA secretary Sibi George said law enforcement cooperation was an “important topic of discussion and an important aspect of the relationship with Belgium”.“All issues of concern and interest are discussed at all levels of our engagement ... India remains committed to ensuring that fugitives are brought back to the country to face the law,” he added.Modi said ties with Belgium had expanded beyond traditional sectors. “Defence and security cooperation is a key pillar of our relationship. Today, we agreed to enhance military exchanges and training cooperation between the two countries,” said the PM. “The agreements between our govts and defence industries will open up opportunities for defence co-development and co-production. We will also further strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation between our agencies to combat crime,” he added.PM said unprecedented cooperation, including the recently concluded FTA between India and EU – two of the world’s largest democratic blocs – would give a boost to global stability, development and shared prosperity.The leaders also discussed Ukraine and West Asia, underlining their support for the rule of law, dialogue and diplomacy. In a joint statement, they stressed the importance of ensuring the safety and security of maritime routes and maintaining safe and unimpeded maritime shipping.“Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we support all efforts aimed at an early end to conflicts and the restoration of peace,” the PM added.The leaders called for closer partnerships in semiconductor technologies to create resilient and advanced technology ecosystems in both countries, with Modi saying that Belgium’s expertise in semiconductors and India’s scale complement each other.The two leaders agreed to soon conclude a migration and mobility agreement to facilitate talent mobility.Belgium also expressed solidarity with India in the fight against terrorism. De Wever condemned the attack on civilians at Pahalgam in April 2025. “Both leaders underscored their commitment to a comprehensive/global approach to counterterrorism and affirmed that terrorism, in any form and manifestation and anywhere, could never be justified and called for its perpetrators to be held accountable in accordance with the law,” said the statement.The leaders also focused on clean energy, critical minerals and reliable supply chains. “The MoU on Renewable Energy signed today will give momentum to our sustainability cooperation. In critical minerals, we have decided to enhance ties in processing & recycling,” PM said.
Article Summary: India and belgium signed deals to deepen defence and clean-energy ties. Pm narendra modi announced a mechanism to fast-track investment between the two countries. De wever’s visit resulted in 10 major outcomes — five mous, including two to boost indigenous defence manufacturing, co-design and co-development.

Article Title: Watch: 2 workers make it out alive 9 days after Nepal floods hit hydropower tunnel
Article Text:
The rescue of two workers have revived hope for hundreds of others still said to be trapped

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be prioritized in Nepal's recovery plan? Infrastructure rebuilding Financial aid for affected families Long-term disaster preparedness Environmental restoration 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Rescuers in Nepal pulled two workers alive from a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Friday, nine days after devastating floods and landslides trapped hundreds of workers inside tunnels across several hydropower sites.The rescue brought a dramatic breakthrough to a desperate operation, but hopes of finding more survivors rose further after rescuers heard voices coming from inside the tunnel, according to Bipin Regmi, police chief in the flood-hit district of Nuwakot.“Rescuers heard voices,” Regmi told CNN, adding that a medical team was on its way to the site.The two workers were pulled out in quick succession from inside the Trishuli 3A plant, where rescuers have been boring into a tunnel in an effort to reach 42 workers who had remained unaccounted for.Video showed about a dozen rescuers pulling one man through a small opening in the ground and clapping as he emerged. The mud-covered worker was then carried away on a rescuer’s shoulder, while a medical team checked on him.Nepal Army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet confirmed the first rescue during the operation. Nepal lawmaker Shri Ram Neupane later said a second worker had also been rescued alive.The tunnel leading to the underground powerhouse is more than 4 kilometres (2.5 miles) long.Dozens of workers were inside when the catastrophic flooding hit the area.About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, according to local authorities, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped inside tunnels. Among those unaccounted for are workers from China, South Korea and India.Read more: Nepal estimates $2.56 billion flood damage, faces $52.6 million recovery cost The rescue effort has continued under treacherous conditions since Aug. 26, when massive floods and landslides tore through parts of Nepal, likely after a glacier collapse. At least 1,259 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing, according to Nepal’s disaster management agency.On the Tibet side of the border, China said late Wednesday that 21 people had been killed and 541 were missing.The chances of finding survivors have become increasingly uncertain with each passing day. Indian Army Colonel Parikshit Mehra, who was involved in the rescue operation at the Trishuli 3A site, said earlier this week that the first 48 hours are the most crucial in a tunnel rescue.“People who are stuck tend to panic much more than when they are outside in the open,” Mehra told CNN’s Anderson Cooper.“Getting stuck in a tunnel you can’t see anything. Generally if you stay in the dark you get disoriented in about 24-25 hours,” he said.“Beyond that, (after) 48 hours, you start hallucinating. And then I think from there on it’s always a fight.”Yet, even as the operation entered its ninth day, Mehra offered a note of hope saying, “There have been miracles.”Also read: Nepal minister goes back on flash flood 'compensation' claim The flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, caused widespread destruction across northern and central Nepal, killing at least 1,282 people and leaving thousands missing. Nepal Police said the highest number of recovered bodies were reported from Chitwan, Nawalparasi East and West, Nuwakot and Rasuwa, with rescue and recovery operations continuing across the affected areas.
Article Summary: Rescuers in nepal pull two workers alive from a tunnel at the trishuli 3a hydropower project. The rescue brought a dramatic breakthrough to a desperate operation, but hopes of finding more survivors rose further. At least 1,259 people have been killed and more than 5,000 remain missing.

Article Title: Estonia minister quits after €70-million Ukraine shell deal involving Indian firm
Article Text:
Estonia minister quits in India-linked row

Estonia’s defence minister Hanno Pevkur has resigned over an arms deal to supply artillery shells to Ukraine using €70 million in European Union funds and involving Indian company, Euronews reported.It emerged on Wednesday that Estonia had paid the amount upfront for the shells, but the Indian company Neco Defence Munitions involved had no previous record of selling artillery ammunition.Estonian newspaper Eesti Ekspress reported that in 2024, Estonia signed a shell-supply deal with Italian-registered Datasel, owned by Indian company Neco Defence Munitions.Neither company had previously manufactured shells.The 2024 deal is now being challenged by Estonia in an arbitration case.Pevkur, who has been defence minister since 2022, said he was taking political responsibility for the controversy.“Although the minister does not count socks and ammunition or conduct contract negotiations, the National Audit Office’s criticisms, primarily concerning the activities of the Defence Forces and the Centre for Defence Investments, raise the question of political responsibility,” Pevkur said.The minister said he had not read the contracts, as defence ministers do not usually handle individual arms deals.“The defence minister does not conduct contract negotiations. The defence minister does not count socks and ammunition,” Pevkur said, adding: “The defence minister makes the fundamental decision to support Ukraine.”Pevkur’s resignation comes as the Russia-Ukraine war has already lasted longer than World War I, with no clear signs of peace or a return to normalcy.
Article Summary: Estonia’s defence minister hanno pevkur has resigned over an arms deal to supply artillery shells to ukraine using €70 million in european union funds. It emerged on wednesday that estonia had paid the amount upfront for the shells, but the indian company involved had no previous record of selling artillery ammunition.

Article Title: China’s grey-zone game: Why India must prepare for ‘armed coexistence’
Article Text:
India-China ties have thawed since the border skirmish in 2020.

Former foreign secretary

Vijay Gokhale

argues that China waits for a strategic opening, acts pre-emptively and then builds a narrative of self-defence.

His new book, “China’s Wars: The Politics and Diplomacy Behind its Military Coercion”, examines past conflicts and China’s recent grey-zone tactics.

In an interview with Indrajeet Rai, Gokhale explains why the

India-China relationship

has entered an era of “armed coexistence”, why a full-scale war is not the most likely outcome but cannot be ruled out, and how political uncertainty after Xi Jinping could produce global economic shocks or military adventurism.

You describe China as an opportunistic power. What does that mean, and when does Beijing decide to act pre-emptively?

China often depicts its own aggressive action as defensive and blames the other side. How central is this narrative warfare to its strategy?

China’s grey-zone strategy seeks to steadily pressure and exhaust rivals while avoiding the escalation of tensions into full-scale war.

You argue that China is pursuing sustained grey-zone coercion. How does this work against India?

Does that mean a large-scale India-China war is unlikely in the foreseeable future?

China’s capabilities against Taiwan have grown, while the US is distracted by several conflicts. Could Xi Jinping move on Taiwan to secure his legacy?

Edited excerpts:By opportunistic power, I did not intend to suggest that China is very different from other major powers. In the case studies in my book, China waited for the international situation to turn favourable, or for some advantage to accrue from its relations with other major powers, before carrying out conflict with a neighbour or another country. It used opportunity strategically to achieve its goals.The Chinese idea of preventive deterrence or preventive conflict differs from the Western concept. In the West, deterrence is a counteraction intended to stop the adversary from escalating. In the Chinese context, it is pre-emptive: China acts even before the adversary has had the chance to act first. The aim is to deliver a political and psychological shock so the adversary desists or fears retaliation.The 1962 conflict is one example. There was no indication that India intended to launch a military assault. But China used the words of then PM Jawaharlal Nehru and an international situation dominated by the Cuban missile crisis to act pre-emptively against India.The Chinese Communist Party utilised China’s difficult circumstances after the collapse of the empire and projected itself as the only organisation capable of pulling the country out of its problems. It placed the blame for China’s declining economy and global influence on external circumstances. It played the victim’s card: China was perennially the victim, and the party was the instrument that would restore it as a major power.The blame, therefore, was always placed on somebody else: The colonial powers, the United States in the Korean War, India in the 1962 war and the Soviet Union in the 1969 conflict. There was never an acknowledgement that some responsibility also fell on China.This is not limited to foreign policy. The party does not take responsibility for major domestic failures either: The Great Leap Forward, the Cultural Revolution or the 1989 Tiananmen incident. Blame falls on an external force or a few bad elements, never the party itself.Since 1979, China has not fought a real conflict. The leadership made economic development the priority, and successive leaders after Mao Zedong focused on reform and opening up.But China was not willing to give up the use of force; it changed the manner in which force was used. Instead of hot wars or major conflict, it engaged and continues to engage in very low-intensity military conflict, popularly known as grey-zone warfare.Grey-zone warfare uses threats or actual force while staying below the threshold that might tempt the rival to launch a counteroffensive. It punishes or deters, but stops short of making the rival feel compelled to push back with force. We see it along the Line of Actual Control, in the South China Sea and in the East China Sea.I have characterised the situation on the LAC after 2020 as the end of peaceful coexistence and the beginning of armed coexistence. Armed coexistence does not mean conflict. It means China will continue to take grey-zone military action around the LAC to keep us tied down and to exhaust us not only financially - because keeping forces and equipment at those heights costs a lot - but also in terms of men and material.This fulfils a key Chinese objective: Keeping India confined to South Asia.Apart from the United States, there are few potential rivals in this century, and India is one. If you look at India, it's geographical location, its population size, its territorial size, its talent, it's economic potential. All of it lends a credence to the belief that India can become a major power in this century. And clearly, China would like to delay that possibility.Nobody can predict this definitively. China and its decision-making processes are opaque, and there are no alternative channels of information such as free media or civil society.China is a mature state focused on becoming the strongest economy and power in the world. On a rational cost-benefit analysis, the price of a major war with India could exceed the benefits. Logically, China would be reluctant to engage in such a conflict.At the end of the day, however, it is impossible to predict. We have to be prepared for the worst, while logically understanding that a hot conflict with India may not be in China’s interest in the foreseeable future.An American commander of the Indo-Pacific Command, Admiral Philip Davidson, suggested that by 2027 China would have the military capability to launch an assault on Taiwan. Some interpreted that to mean China would attack by 2027, but he did not actually say this.China’s capabilities for an assault on an island have substantially increased: Landing craft, area-denial capabilities, communication systems and anti-ship missiles.It is one thing for a major power to bomb another country and destroy its infrastructure, and quite another to occupy or conquer it. That requires a very large commitment of forces and material, with no assured guarantee of victory.China’s demographic decline is already causing anxiety. An assault would mean mass casualties because boots on the ground would be required. After Galwan, India acknowledged within days that 20 soldiers had been martyred; China took much longer to admit fatalities. With Taiwan potentially producing casualties in the hundreds or thousands, Beijing will worry about the domestic impact.This is where democracy, for all its weaknesses, becomes a strength. A democratic government has electoral and constitutional legitimacy to act, including in war. In China, the party claims it has popular support but has never tested that proposition. The reaction to large-scale war casualties is unpredictable.Deng Xiaoping introduced two reforms that stabilised succession: Those above 68 could not continue in top party positions, and the president was limited to two five-year terms. This helped ensure smooth transitions from Jiang Zemin to Hu Jintao and then to Xi Jinping.Xi has abolished the age and term limits. In an authoritarian system, no leader will voluntarily give up power because enemies may find it easier to target him, and he cannot be certain a successor will not misuse authority against him.China could enter a period of political uncertainty and potentially turmoil as Xi ages and factions emerge in a contest for power. It is unclear whether this happens before or after his death, or whether he intends to stand for a fourth term.Because China is the world’s second-largest economy, domestic turmoil would affect its economy, military and diplomacy and create huge ripple effects abroad. Beleaguered regimes also sometimes use an external threat to divert attention. India must consider whether turmoil could produce military adventurism and how to preserve its national interests, sovereignty and territorial integrity.China lacks the United States’ large network of treaty allies. But we should not underestimate the goodwill it enjoys. The Belt and Road Initiative has been welcomed as an alternative route to development. Western assistance often came with harsh conditions; China offers fewer and less onerous strings. Nobody gives aid for free, but China has built substantial diplomatic influence.There was little need for China to do more in the Iran war. It could neither persuade the United States to stop nor force peace. It protected its oil interests and relations with Iran and the Gulf countries without entering the mediation game.When the conflict ends, Iran will rebuild using its oil and gas wealth. It is unlikely to trust the West, while China can build infrastructure at a scale few others can match. China needs energy; Iran needs infrastructure and money. That creates an enormous downstream economic opportunity and a win-win situation. Why would China get significantly involved now when there seems to be no clear way out of the conflict?India should not look at the world order through an either-or lens. The United States and China will both remain major powers. The question is how, in a triangular or quadrangular relationship, including the European Union if it acts as a union, we create an international framework relevant to this century.India has objective advantages: Its location, demographics and consumer base; tested political stability; an independent military capability and growing defence industry; and talent.I do not see how India can fail to become a major power in this century. The international order is disintegrating and all states are hedging their bets; India is doing so too. The task is not to choose a US-led or China-led order. It is to help build an order in which India is one of the leaders.

Article Title: 'Shared commitment to eradicate terrorism': PM Modi as India, Belgium sign key MoUs

NEW DELHI: India and Belgium on Thursday signed a series of MoUs and agreements aimed at expanding bilateral cooperation across renewable energy, defence, trade, investment, maritime affairs, critical minerals, semiconductors and research, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Belgian Prime Minister Bart De Wever held talks in New Delhi.The agreements were exchanged in the presence of PM Modi and De Wever at Hyderabad House, with the two sides seeking to turn the longstanding India-Belgium relationship into a broader strategic and economic partnership.PM Modi said the two countries had agreed to strengthen cooperation in several emerging areas, including startups, maritime capacity building, universities and research, while also working towards a Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement to facilitate the movement of talent."Today, we agreed to strengthen connections between our startups and enhance capacity building in the maritime sector. We will also reinforce cooperation in the university and research sectors, and we will soon sign a Migration and Mobility Partnership Agreement to facilitate the movement of talent. Today we also held detailed discussions on regional and global developments. Both India and Belgium believe in the rule of law, dialogue, and diplomacy..."The Prime Minister also highlighted the renewable energy MoU signed during the visit, saying it would provide fresh momentum to bilateral cooperation on sustainability. The two countries have additionally decided to enhance cooperation in the processing and recycling of critical minerals."Defence and security cooperation is a key pillar of our relationship. Today, we have agreed to enhance military exchanges and training cooperation between the two countries. Agreements reached between our governments and defence industries will open up new opportunities for defence co-development and co-production. We will also further strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation against crime between our respective agencies. A clean energy future and reliable supply chains are our shared priorities. The MoU on renewable energy signed today will give new momentum to our cooperation on sustainability. We have decided to enhance cooperation in the processing and recycling of critical minerals. Belgium's expertise in semiconductors and India's scale complement each other; in this regard, we will work together to integrate Belgium's IMEC Institute with India's semiconductor ecosystem. People-to-people ties are the greatest strength of our relationship."The two sides also discussed ways to strengthen economic ties following the conclusion of the India-European Union Free Trade Agreement earlier this year. PM Modi said India and Belgium had taken several steps to translate the opportunities created by the agreement into concrete economic outcomes."Earlier this year, we concluded a historic Free Trade Agreement between India and the European Union. This unprecedented cooperation between two of the world's largest democratic powers will further strengthen global stability, growth, and shared prosperity. India's sustained economic progress and this agreement have opened up new possibilities for our economic ties. Today, we have taken several significant steps to translate these possibilities into concrete results. We have established an 'Investment Fast-Track Mechanism' in India for Belgian companies. We have decided to make the India-Belgium Business Forum a regular mechanism. We will enhance synergy between the financial, fintech, and regulatory institutions of both nations, and through these measures, we will realize the goal of doubling bilateral trade over the next five years"Defence cooperation emerged as another key component of the agreements and discussions. PM Modi said India and Belgium had agreed to increase military exchanges and training, while government and defence industry agreements would create opportunities for co-development and co-production of defence equipment.He also said the two countries would strengthen intelligence sharing and cooperation between their agencies to combat crime.PM Modi said India and Belgium were also working together on modern defence equipment and cited the Zorawar tank as an example of the expanding partnership."I had the opportunity to visit Belgium ten years ago, and I am delighted to see the remarkable progress our partnership has made over the past decade. Today, the scope of our cooperation has expanded beyond traditional sectors to encompass strategic areas such as defense and clean energy. We are collaborating on modern defence equipment, such as the Zorawar tank. We are also developing one of the world's largest green ammonia projects in Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh. "On clean energy and technology, PM Modi said the renewable energy agreement would strengthen cooperation on sustainability, while the proposed integration of Belgium's IMEC Institute with India's semiconductor ecosystem would combine Belgian expertise with India's scale.The two countries also discussed critical minerals, particularly their processing and recycling, as both sides look to build more reliable supply chains.PM Modi said the latest agreements marked an expansion of ties beyond traditional areas such as diamonds and trade."Last month, Belgium and the Netherlands jointly hosted the Hockey World Cup. I extend my heartiest congratulations to you for the magnificent organization of this World Cup. I also commend our players for their hard work and performance. Diamonds have long linked India and Belgium. Today, we are transforming this historic bond into a comprehensive partnership. I am confident that our discussions today mark the beginning of a new chapter in our bilateral relations. .."The Prime Minister also placed the bilateral engagement in the context of ongoing global conflicts and geopolitical uncertainty, saying India and Belgium supported efforts towards peace while sharing a commitment to combating terrorism."... Whether it is Ukraine or West Asia, we support all efforts towards an early end to conflict and the establishment of peace; furthermore, eradicating terrorism in all its forms is our shared commitment. Last month, Belgium and the Netherlands jointly hosted the Hockey World Cup. I extend my heartiest congratulations to you for the magnificent organization of this World Cup. I also commend our players for their hard work and performance. Diamonds have long linked India and Belgium. Today, we are transforming this historic bond into a comprehensive partnership. I am confident that our discussions today mark the beginning of a new chapter in our bilateral relations..."PM Modi said the broader global environment remained challenging, with conflicts affecting food and fuel security as well as supply chains. He said India's economy had continued to maintain its momentum despite the uncertainty."The world is currently going through a period of great upheaval. Conflict situations persist in various parts of the globe, and uncertainty is impacting sectors ranging from food and fuel to supply chains. Even amidst this challenging environment, the Indian economy has maintained its momentum; we recorded a growth rate of 7.8% in the last quarter. Today, India's growth story is becoming a source of confidence and new opportunities for the world. "The agreements and discussions came during De Wever's first visit to India as Belgian Prime Minister. He is in the country from September 2 to 4 at the invitation of PM Modi. His visit is also the first by a Belgian Prime Minister to India in two decades.De Wever, who took office in February 2025, is accompanied by Belgium's Minister of Defence and Foreign Trade, Theo Francken, along with a high-level delegation of officials and business leaders, including representatives from the Belgian defence industry.Earlier on Thursday, Francken held the India-Belgium Defence Ministers' Meeting with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, where both sides discussed expanding defence cooperation and greater engagement between their defence industries."The world is witnessing a time of great geopolitical and economic turmoil. Most of it is not our doing, but we have to handle the challenges. In such situations, meeting a friend and partner like you provides a useful opportunity to exchange views and perspectives," Singh said.Singh said the recently held India-Belgium Strategic Dialogue had provided a framework for taking the bilateral partnership forward, particularly in defence and security."We welcome greater cooperation with Belgian and Indian defence companies," he said.Francken, meanwhile, called for deeper cooperation with India, highlighting the country's technological capabilities and saying Belgium needed partners such as India for future projects."We can learn so much from you. You are a high-technology country. You are one of the most densely populated countries, and we really need to work together because Belgium is an old Western European country with a lot of technology, but we need countries like India. We need to collaborate on future projects, and for Belgium, this is the way forward"Francken also referred to Belgium's economic mission to India led by Princess Astrid in March 2025, describing it as a first step towards a renewed relationship between the two countries.He said the mission had helped generate momentum in bilateral ties, with contracts being signed on collaboration projects within 18 months."That is amazing. This means that we worked hard, that our people worked hard, and that we can go further in this pathway."The Belgian minister also said De Wever's visit had a packed agenda focused on expanding bilateral cooperation."I'm very happy to be here with our Prime Minister. For first time in more than 20 years a Belgian Prime Minister is visiting your beautiful country. We have a busy, busy schedule with lot of signing ceremonies, a lot of good talks with the Prime Minister…"Francken said Belgium and India could address the geopolitical challenges facing the world through greater friendship and partnership."I think it's totally right when you talk about geopolitical challenges that we have to meet. We didn't organise them, we didn't always want them, but we need to be realistic, and we need to go further. And we can do this in friendship and partnership between Belgium and India."The latest agreements build on growing economic engagement between the two countries. A Belgian Economic Mission led by Princess Astrid in March 2025 brought together 338 participants from companies, chambers of commerce, academia and public institutions and resulted in 38 MoUs.De Wever also paid tributes to Mahatma Gandhi at Rajghat on Thursday, where he laid a wreath and offered flowers before signing the visitor's book.The Belgian Prime Minister's visit is aimed at further strengthening bilateral ties and expanding cooperation across trade, investment, defence, technology and connectivity, while also giving fresh momentum to India's engagement with the European Union and Europe.

The two sides sought to turn the longstanding india-belgium relationship into a broader strategic and economic partnership. Pm modi said the two countries had agreed to strengthen cooperation in several emerging areas.

Article Title: Nepal flash floods: Relatives hold symbolic funerals for thousands missing as toll crosses 1,243
Article Text:
The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region rose to 1,243 on Thursday.

The death toll from devastating flash floods in the Nepal-Tibet region rose to 1,243 on Thursday, as rescue teams battled heavy rain and thick debris while searching for people believed to be trapped in tunnels and underground power facilities along the Bhotekoshi River.Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Nepal must raise the disaster’s connection to climate change with the international community, as families held symbolic funerals for relatives who remain missing following last week’s floods.Speaking at the fifth daily press briefing in Kathmandu, ministry of foreign affairs spokesperson Lok Bahadur Chhetri said authorities had begun conducting temporary burials for victims as search and rescue operations continued around the clock.Chhetri said 11,993 people had been rescued, while 1,114 bodies had been recovered. Around 3,900 people remain unaccounted for, he said, urging relatives of those missing to provide DNA samples at the Nepal Police Hospital in Maharajgunj or their nearest District Police Office to help forensic teams with identification.He also outlined international assistance being provided to Nepal. A 19-member forensic team from India is working with Nepal Police on DNA analysis, while specialised teams and equipment have also arrived from China, Singapore and South Korea to support identification and recovery efforts.Rescue teams from the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force are working with international specialists from India, China and South Korea to clear mud, debris and boulders from underground hydropower facilities in areas including Langtang, Chilime and Upper Trisuli.According to the ANI report, more than 300 foreign nationals have been safely rescued, while around 590 citizens from 34 countries remain unaccounted for.Working with Chinese authorities, Nepal has also helped evacuate about 2,500 pilgrims returning from Mount Kailash through the Hilsa and Tatopani border crossings and via air routes through Lhasa. Efforts are also underway to clear stranded cargo and assist Nepali nationals near the Kerung border.Addressing Parliament earlier Wednesday, Prime Minister Balendra Shah said the catastrophic August 26 Bhotekoshi River floods, triggered by a high-altitude Himalayan avalanche, underscored the growing threat posed by climate change across the region.Shah said nearly 4,000 people remain missing across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading, stressing that addressing the effects of climate change requires a collective global effort.As Nepal continues to coordinate international assistance from India, China, the United States, Japan, the Asian Development Bank, the World Bank, the European Union and the United Nations, authorities are deploying available resources toward emergency relief, searches for missing people and long-term recovery.According to Nepal Police, 348 bodies were recovered in Chitwan, 217 in Nawalparasi East, 190 in Nawalparasi West and 155 in Nuwakot. Another 66 bodies were recovered in Gorkha, 59 in Dhading, 45 in Rasuwa and 38 in Tanahu.A total of 7,912 police personnel have been deployed to flood-hit areas to assist with search and rescue operations, distribute relief supplies and manage recovered bodies.Authorities have also published details of 911 unidentified bodies on the Nepal Police website to help families identify missing relatives.Meanwhile, rainwater accumulating inside a hydropower tunnel has created additional difficulties for search and rescue teams working in areas affected by the Bhotekoshi floods, said Dharma Raj Uprety, executive chief of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA).Search operations have been particularly challenging because of the hazardous conditions inside the project’s tunnels. Teams from the Nepali Army and Armed Police Force, along with foreign technical experts and project employees, are continuing efforts to locate workers who remain missing.As per the PTI report, Ganesh Karki, former president of the Independent Power Producers’ Association, Nepal (IPPAN), said rescue operations have also been slowed by difficulties transporting heavy equipment to the tunnels.
